facts.value: Uses Dahua protocol (Amcrest standard). Portrait 3:4 aspect ratio , set detect to 720x960. Community favorite for local-only doorbell with Frigate. Button press exposed as Dahua event (AccessControl/CallNoAnswered). go2rtc backchannel (append to the go2rtc stream URL): #backchannel=0 = two-way audio off, normal button/chime behavior (recommended default , go2rtc otherwise auto-opens the Dahua backchannel, which can disrupt the doorbell); #backchannel=1 = two-way audio on, requires extra setup (e.g. github.com/RobTheBuilder2/amcrest-intercom).

facts.value: Dual-channel , configure as TWO Frigate cameras: panoramic = channel=1 (3840x1080, 32:9 , set detect to 1280x360 to match), PTZ = channel=2 (2560x1440, rtsp://{user}:{pass}@{ip}:554/cam/realmonitor?channel=2&subtype=0, detect 1280x720). For ONVIF autotracking on the PTZ channel add 'onvif: {host, port: 80, user, password, autotracking: {enabled: true}}'. Note: powered by DC 36V, not PoE.

records.name: Kedacom IPC121-Ei7N
notes: Recognitive (character/plate) indoor box camera, C/CS-mount (lens not included), visible 2.0MP sensor. Not thermal; no IR illuminator.

records.name: Kedacom IPC123-Ei7N
notes: Recognitive indoor box camera, C/CS-mount (lens not included), visible 2.0MP sensor. Not thermal; ICR day/night, no IR illuminator.

records.name: Kedacom IPC123-Fi4N
notes: Face-recognitive indoor box camera (60fps), C/CS-mount (lens not included), visible 2.0MP sensor. Not thermal; no IR illuminator. Distinct from IPC123-Ei7N.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2131-AN-IR1
notes: IR1 = manual varifocal, IR2 = motorized varifocal (identical optics/sensor). IR 20-40m.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2131-DN-IR
notes: IR1: 2.7-9mm manual varifocal; IR2: 2.7-9mm motorized varifocal. 26 IR LEDs.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2231-DN
notes: Variants: L1 (2.7-9mm manual varifocal), L2 (2.7-9mm motorized varifocal), L3 (2.2mm CS mount, 129 deg), L4 (2.0mm M12, 149 deg).

records.name: Kedacom IPC2241-FN-SIR
notes: IPC2241-FN-SIR is wired-only; IPC2241-FNW-SIR variant adds a Wi-Fi module.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2451-Fi4N/Fi4NB-SIR50
notes: Human-recognitive IR bullet with face capture, visible 4.0MP sensor. Not thermal. Two lens options: Z2812 (2.8-12mm) and Z8032 (8-32mm). Smart IR up to 50m.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2655-Gi4N
notes: Human-recognitive IR bullet with face/character capture, visible 6.0MP sensor. Not thermal. Smart IR up to 100m. IR variant of IPC2655-Gi7N (white-light).

records.name: Kedacom IPC2655-Gi7N
notes: Face/human & vehicle recognitive (capture) bullet. White-light LED for color night vision (~30m), not thermal. 6.0MP visible CMOS.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2833-Fi4N-SIR50-Z6022
notes: Recognitive vandal-resistant (IK10) semi-dome with face capture, visible 8.0MP (4K) sensor. Not thermal. Smart IR 20-50m, 120dB WDR.

records.name: Kedacom IPC2855-Gi4N
notes: Human-recognitive IR bullet with face capture, visible 8.0MP (4K) sensor. Not thermal. Smart IR 80-100m.

records.name: Kedacom IPC442-i405-NP
notes: Recognitive PTZ speed dome with face recognition, visible 4.0MP sensor (1080p main stream). Not thermal.

records.name: Reolink E1 Pro
notes: Field of view (82° horizontal / 43° vertical) sourced from Reolink's official E1 Pro datasheet PDF, which describes an earlier hardware revision (4MP, F2.4 lens, 256GB max microSD) than the unit currently sold on reolink.com/product/e1-pro/ (5MP, F1.6 lens, 512GB max microSD). Focal length and sensor size are unchanged between revisions, so FOV is assumed to carry over; all other specs in this entry reflect the current live product page.

facts.value: Detect width/height match the sub-stream (/Preview_01_sub), which on the E1 Zoom is locked at 640x480 , set these to your camera's actual sub-stream resolution so Frigate isn't resizing every frame. Use the official /Preview_01_main path (Reolink RTSP KB); it serves the stream at the codec configured in the camera. records.name: Reolink E1 Zoom
notes: Reolink relaunched E1 Zoom as a 4K/8MP Wi-Fi 6 model (3840x2160), superseding the original 5MP (2560x1920) version this entry previously described. Field of view is not published for the current unit on reolink.com/product/e1-zoom/ (the prior '95-34 horizontal' figure could not be re-confirmed for the new hardware and has been removed rather than carried forward). Video codec is likewise not stated on the current product page and has been left unset.

For Reolink, the HTTP-FLV streams tend to be more reliable in Frigate than RTSP (which can stall / throw non-monotonic-timestamp errors); go2rtc can use the http source and add a secondary RTSP stream only for audio.

records.name: Reolink FE-P
notes: Launched 2023-05-31 as Reolink's first fisheye camera line (FE-P PoE / FE-W WiFi). Indoor use only per official product page (do not install outdoors); no official IP rating is published, so ip_rating has been left unset rather than guessed. Reolink marketed the FE-P as ONVIF-compliant, but per Reolink's own community forum, ONVIF certification applies only to firmware v3.0.0.1987_23041503 or later , earlier firmware may misbehave with third-party ONVIF NVRs.

facts.label: Home Assistant notes

Check the camera's hardware version before assuming local/standalone access works.

facts.label: Frigate notes
facts.value: Portrait 3:4 aspect ratio (white model 1920x2560, black model is 4:3 at 2560x1920). Set detect to 720x960 for white or 960x720 for black to maintain correct ratio. For two-way audio: use go2rtc as the RTSP proxy , Frigate does not natively handle talk-back. In go2rtc config add the camera as an RTSP source, then enable WebRTC with opus re-encoding for the back-channel: 'streams: doorbell: - rtsp://{user}:{pass}@{ip}:554/h264Preview_01_main - ffmpeg:doorbell#audio=opus'. Button press events are not exposed via RTSP; use HA Reolink integration's Visitor binary_sensor or subscribe to ONVIF events via MQTT.

facts.label: Frigate notes
facts.value: Standard Tapo wired-camera RTSP scheme (stream1 main / stream2 sub); not individually bench-tested on this model. go2rtc alternative: TP-Link's proprietary protocol via go2rtc (tapo://<tapo-account-password>@{ip}) is often more stable than RTSP (fewer timeouts / non-monotonic-timestamp errors). The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) , see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). Pan/tilt: Tapo exposes ONVIF PTZ on port 2020 (not 80) , point Frigate's onvif block at host:<ip> port:2020 with the camera Account credentials for manual pan/tilt. (Frigate autotracking stays off: Tapo only does continuous-move ONVIF, no reliable absolute/FOV positioning.)

The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) , see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). Pan/tilt: Tapo exposes ONVIF PTZ on port 2020 (not 80) , point Frigate's onvif block at host:<ip> port:2020 with the camera Account credentials for manual pan/tilt. (Frigate autotracking stays off: Tapo only does continuous-move ONVIF, no reliable absolute/FOV positioning.)

The password form is firmware-dependent: either your Tapo app/cloud account password, or user `admin` + the UPPERCASE SHA-256 of the camera password (`tapo://admin:<UPPERCASE-SHA256>@{ip}`) , see go2rtc's Tapo docs. It is not the camera's plain RTSP/Device password. If non-monotonic-timestamp errors persist, disable audio for that camera in Frigate. Chrome may render the go2rtc live view with a squashed aspect ratio (a browser live-view quirk, not the stream); Firefox is correct. The go2rtc tapo:// source also carries a two-way-audio backchannel, so Frigate's live view gets a talk button (mic+speaker). Pan/tilt: Tapo exposes ONVIF PTZ on port 2020 (not 80) , point Frigate's onvif block at host:<ip> port:2020 with the camera Account credentials for manual pan/tilt. (Frigate autotracking stays off: Tapo only does continuous-move ONVIF, no reliable absolute/FOV positioning.)
